title: Affine chart dictionary for local-map approximation
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ have common image $s\in S$. Suppose $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. There are affine open neighbourhoods $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$, $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ of $x$, and $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$ of $y$, with both structure maps landing in $S_0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], having the following properties. The rings $R,A,B$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A,B$ are finitely generated $R$-algebras, and $B=R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)$ for finite $n,m\geq0$, where the polynomial ring is the iterated polynomial ring of [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. If $\mathfrak r,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ are the primes representing $s,x,y$, then $\mathfrak p\cap R=\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak r$, and the canonical identifications $R_{\mathfrak r}=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $A_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ respect the structure maps; $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

For any étale ring homomorphism $h:A\to A'$ and prime $\mathfrak p'\subset A'$ with $h^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak p$, the ring $A'$ is Noetherian. For every $R$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:B\to A'$ with $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak q$, the maps $\operatorname{Spec}h$, $\operatorname{Spec}\phi$, composed with the above open inclusions, define morphisms $p_U:U=\operatorname{Spec}A'\to X$ and $f_U:U\to Y$ over $S$, with $p_U(\mathfrak p')=x$ and $f_U(\mathfrak p')=y$. The morphism $p_U$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]; if $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is an isomorphism then so is $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Under $\mathcal O_{U,\mathfrak p'}=A'_{\mathfrak p'}$, the stalk maps are exactly the localizations $h_{\mathfrak p}:A_{\mathfrak p}\to A'_{\mathfrak p'}$ and $\phi_{\mathfrak q}:B_{\mathfrak q}\to A'_{\mathfrak p'}$. Their induced maps on maximal-ideal completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion-map-local] and their completion maps agree under these identifications, and $\mathfrak m_{U,\mathfrak p'}^N\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,\mathfrak p'}$ identifies with $(\mathfrak p'A'_{\mathfrak p'})^N\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$ for every $N\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, proof, affine reduction in the first paragraph and passage back to spectra in the final sentence; G-ring input: More on Algebra Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, applied over R_r without replacing the affine neighbourhoods by their localizations

proof.text: Choose an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $s$. By the definition of locally finite type, the inverse image of $S_0$ in each of $X,Y$ has an affine cover with finitely generated coordinate algebras over $R$. Choose members containing $x,y$ and call their rings $A,B$. The affine-open Noetherian lemma makes $R$ Noetherian. The finite-type algebra Noetherian lemma then makes $A,B$ Noetherian. Apply the finite-presentation lemma to $R\to B$: a finite generating family $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ gives a surjection $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\to B$ whose kernel has finite generators $F_1,\ldots,F_m$. This is the required presentation, including $n=0$ or $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, first paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 00FN and 00FP (3)

proof.text: Use the canonical affine open immersions and their stalk identifications to write $\mathcal O_{S,s}=R_{\mathfrak r}$, $\mathcal O_{X,x}=A_{\mathfrak p}$, and $\mathcal O_{Y,y}=B_{\mathfrak q}$. Compatibility of a sheaf morphism with restrictions sends the germ of $r\in R$ to the germ of its structural image. Since stalk maps are local, the inverse images of the maximal ideals are the maximal ideal of $R_{\mathfrak r}$; pulling back further to $R$ gives $\mathfrak p\cap R=\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak r$. Every localized element is a fraction, so the stalk maps necessarily send $r/t$ to its structural image divided by that of $t$. Thus these identifications respect both structure maps.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6), and the definition of stalk maps of locally ringed spaces

proof.text: Transfer the assumed G-ring structure to $R_{\mathfrak r}$ by the ring-equivalence lemma. Put $M=\operatorname{im}(R\setminus\mathfrak r)\subset A$ and $C=M^{-1}A$. The images of a finite set of $R$-algebra generators of $A$ generate $C$ over $R_{\mathfrak r}$: a fraction $a/t$ is the polynomial expression for $a$ with its coefficients divided by $t$. Consequently the finite-type G-ring ascent theorem applies to $R_{\mathfrak r}\to C$ and makes $C$ a G-ring. The prime $P=\mathfrak pC$ is proper since $M\cap\mathfrak p=\varnothing$. The maps $C_P\to A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $A_{\mathfrak p}\to C_P$ send fractions to the same fractions and are inverse: precisely all elements of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ have been inverted.

source.place: Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring; applied after localizing the base at r, as needed in Tag 0CAU

proof.text: The localization $C_P$ is Noetherian by the localization Noetherian lemma. For a prime $Q$ of $C_P$, let $Q_0$ be its inverse image in $C$. It is contained in $P$, and the fraction maps give $(C_P)_Q\cong C_{Q_0}$, since both invert exactly the complement of $Q_0$. These local ring identifications identify maximal ideals. The completion ring-equivalence lemma supplies compatible identifications of their completions; regular-map invariance therefore transfers regularity of $C_{Q_0}\to\widehat{C_{Q_0}}$ to the completion map of $(C_P)_Q$. Since $Q$ was arbitrary, the definition of a G-ring makes $C_P$ a G-ring. Transfer it along $C_P\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$ using G-ring invariance. This proves the local G-ring assertion without assuming $R$ itself is a G-ring.

source.place: Tag 07PV, proof, first sentence: localization of a G-ring; Definition 07GH, with algebra.tex Tag 00FN

proof.text: For the given $h:A\to A'$, form $U=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $p_U=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}h$, where $\iota_X:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ is the canonical open immersion with image the chart $X_0$ chosen in Step 1. That $h$ is étale means that $\operatorname{Spec}h$ is étale; if it is read instead as an étale ring map in the sense of Algebra 00U1, the étale ring map criterion gives the same conclusion, so both readings agree. The open-immersion clause (1) of the étale permanence lemma makes $\iota_X$ étale, and its composition clause (2) makes $p_U=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}h$ étale. Clause (1) of the étale finite-presentation lemma, applied to $A\to A'$, gives $A'\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ as $A$-algebras; in particular $A'$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra. Since $A$ is Noetherian by Step 1, the finite-type Noetherian lemma makes $A'$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 02GI (definition-etale), 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale); algebra.tex Tag 00U1 (definition-etale: an étale ring map is of finite presentation) and Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence)

proof.text: For the given $R$-algebra map $\phi:B\to A'$, define $f_U=\iota_Y\circ\operatorname{Spec}\phi$. Functoriality of spectra and $\phi\circ(R\to B)=h\circ(R\to A)$ show that the two composites from $U$ to $S_0$ agree, hence that $p_U,f_U$ are over $S$. A spectrum map sends a prime to its inverse image: equivalently, its local stalk map carries a germ into the maximal ideal precisely when the image germ is in the source maximal ideal. The assumed equalities $h^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak p$ and $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak q$ therefore give $p_U(\mathfrak p')=x$ and $f_U(\mathfrak p')=y$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, final sentence; spectra as in schemes.tex Tag 01HV and the construction of Spec of a ring map

proof.text: The affine-open stalk lemma applied also to $U$ gives $\mathcal O_{U,\mathfrak p'}=A'_{\mathfrak p'}$. A stalk map sends the germ of a global section to the germ of its pullback; hence the two maps send $a/1$ to $h(a)/1$ and $b/1$ to $\phi(b)/1$. Their denominators outside $\mathfrak p$ or $\mathfrak q$ have images outside $\mathfrak p'$. Preservation of inverses now gives $a/t\mapsto h(a)/h(t)$ and $b/v\mapsto\phi(b)/\phi(v)$, exactly the two localized maps in the statement. Quotienting these same maps by the maximal ideals identifies the residue-field map of $p_U$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. An isomorphism of the latter thus gives the asserted isomorphism from $\kappa(x)$.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6); fraction description of the induced stalk map and residue field

proof.text: Let $e_V$ denote any of the local ring identifications above. It carries the unique maximal ideal onto the unique maximal ideal, so it induces maps $e_{V,n}$ of the quotients by their $n$-th powers. For either stalk map $g$ and its localized ring map $g_0$, Step 7 gives $e_{U,n}\circ g_n=(g_0)_n\circ e_{V,n}$. The completion-map lemma says that the induced map on completions is exactly $(z_n)_n\mapsto(g_n(z_n))_n$. Consequently the displayed quotient equalities give equality of the completed maps, coordinate by coordinate. The canonical completion map sends $a$ to $(a\bmod\mathfrak m^n)_n$, so it commutes with the same identifications. This proves both compatibilities asserted in the item.

source.place: Tag 07ED; inverse-limit description of completion in algebra.tex Section 00M9

proof.text: Finally $e_U$ sends $\mathfrak m_{U,\mathfrak p'}$ onto $\mathfrak p'A'_{\mathfrak p'}$. Its induced completion isomorphism sends a product of $N$ elements of this ideal times a completed element to the corresponding product of their images times the image completed element. Such finite sums generate the extended $N$-th ideal power on both sides. Applying the inverse isomorphism gives the opposite inclusion. Thus it identifies $\mathfrak m_{U,\mathfrak p'}^N\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,\mathfrak p'}$ with $(\mathfrak p'A'_{\mathfrak p'})^N\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$ for every $N\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, congruence ideal in the proof, under the affine local-ring identification
